journal_entries.description: Borrowed on a one-year, 7% note payable; full proceeds deposited at Crestview National Bank.
Initial recognition reclassification of the legally restricted 8% compensating balance out of unrestricted cash.
Purchased 45-day commercial paper; qualifies as a cash equivalent under the three-month original-maturity policy.
Commercial paper matured; discount interest earned.
Purchased U.S. Treasury bill with two months remaining to maturity; cash equivalent.
Transferred general cash to the restricted dividend fund (dividends payable January 15, Year 2 -> current).
Deposited cash with a trustee for the bond sinking fund; related bonds mature in five years -> noncurrent.
Period-end reclassifying entry: NSF check returned; remove from cash and reinstate the customer receivable.

notes: (i) If the compensating balance had NOT been legally restricted, no reclassification would be made: the $28,800 would stay inside the Crestview checking balance and be reported with Cash (Cash would then be $140,700). Under ASC 210-10-S99-1 the arrangement would instead be described in the notes to the financial statements, disclosing the nature and terms of the compensating-balance arrangement and the amount involved; compensating balances maintained to ensure future credit availability are likewise note-disclosed with their amount and terms. | Part (e) rolls only the listed classification events, as instructed, so it does not tie to the separate Dec 31 item table in part (g). | The 7% note interest is not accrued: the stem limits the events to classification-affecting ones and no Required part asks for it. | The Aug 1 T-bill ($27,000) fails the three-month ORIGINAL-maturity policy and is a short-term investment, excluded from cash equivalents.
